producer_report.summary:
Local checks now take a build slot from a counting queue of `max_check_slots` lock files. This is build job 3 from the design note, local-check part only. The slot is released by Drop, or by the OS if the process dies. The full `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` all passed. The full run came back as success, but its output was too large to read back.

- **Queue (`slots.rs`):** each slot is an exclusive file lock on `slots/slot-<n>.lock`. A waiting request holds a locked ticket under `slots/queue/` (created under a temporary name, locked, then renamed into place). Only the head ticket tries the slot files, ordered by class, then time asked. Ageing moves a request up one class per `build_age_promote_s`. Dead tickets are removed when read. The `stop` closure runs on every poll, so the kill switch still ends a wait. A wait past `build_wait_s` returns `disk::SlotWait`.
- **`SnapExec::exec`:** takes a `Class::Check` slot after the kill-switch check and the first-check disk gate. It holds the slot past the snapshot restore and stamps `queued_s` on the check. A check that waited reads the disk gate once more before it runs, so a long queue wait does not leave a stale free-space reading.
- **Hold (`disk.rs`, `run/mod.rs`, `run/close.rs`):** `SlotWait`, the reason `environment: build slot wait`, `write_slot_hold` / `read_slot_hold`, and `AnyHold` / `read_any_hold` are new. `hold_for_slot_wait` shares one `commit_hold` helper with `hold_for_disk`. The job stays dispatched with its kept candidate, no outcome and no attempt used. `go` on a held job and `status` both read either hold marker through `read_any_hold`.
- **Drain (`athena-cli/src/drain.rs`):** this file was not in the reading's deliverables. Without it, a slot-wait hold would be reported as `environment: low disk`, which would corrupt the "low disk" count the design uses as a metric. The drain now picks the held outcome from the reason: budget short, build slot wait, else low disk.
- **Config:** `PipelineConfig` gains `build_wait_s` (default 1800) and `build_age_promote_s` (default 600). Each must be at least 1, and unknown keys are still refused.
- **Records and status:** `CheckRun.queued_s` is optional and skipped when None, so old records still read. `status` prints a `build wait` line in the throughput section only when some check has a `queued_s`.
- **Compiler-forced edits:** one-line `queued_s: None` additions in checks.rs, routing.rs, verify.rs, introspect.rs, reading.rs, close.rs, send_back.rs, run/mod.rs, run/tests.rs, status.rs, records.rs and the status_durations test.
- **Docs:** CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased > Added. Build job 3 in the design note is marked built, with the choices recorded.

criteria_check.evidence: Ran `cargo test -p athena-core --lib slots::` (the_second_request_waits_then_runs) and the run::tests filter that includes two_jobs_with_one_build_slot_run_one_after_the_other: both passed. The job-level test runs two real `go` calls on two threads at the default limit of 1. It asserts the log order first-start, first-end, second. The first fake waits for the other job's ticket via SlotQueue::waiting(), and the second fake asserts that no check is running. It also asserts both recorded queued_s values are present and the larger one is above zero and above the other.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo test -p athena-core` includes a test where a slot holder's process dies (a child process holding the slot lock is killed, or a holder is dropped on panic/error) and a waiter then acquires the slot with no manual cleanup or sweeper.

open_issues: Open question 1 from the plan, left unresolved (your call): the baseline run (`baseline_checks`) and the 'fails without' reruns (`demonstration_runs`) do not take a build slot. They have no hold path today and the reading names only `SnapExec::exec`. The design note records this.

Open question 2 from the plan, left unresolved (your call): ageing moves a request up one class per `build_age_promote_s` waited, down to the top class, as implemented and recorded in the design note. Only `Class::Check` is requested now, so nothing observable depends on it.

The 250 ms poll means a second request that arrives while the first holds a not-yet-removed ticket can wait one poll even when a second slot is free. This is acceptable now, but the poll interval is a field (`with_poll`) if it needs tuning.
The slot is per check, not per job. A job with several checks (fmt, clippy, test) re-queues between them, so another job's check can run in between. This matches the design's unit of one command.
mistakes: My first slots tests asserted exactly one request had waited with 3 requests on 2 slots, and asserted try_acquire right after a release; both were flaky or wrong. A request queued behind a ticket not yet removed waits one poll even when a slot is free, and parallel tests' forked children can briefly hold a released lock. I weakened the first to a lower bound and added a retry helper for the second.
learnings: `std::fs::File::try_lock` conflicts across separate open file descriptions in one process, so threads and tests share the real lock semantics. A forked child (any test spawning a process or git) briefly holds copies of open lock files, so a release can look delayed by milliseconds. Tests therefore retry try_acquire for a moment (take_soon / take_slot_soon) instead of asserting once.

The libtest harness prints `test <name> ... ` before the test body when run with --nocapture, so a child test's marker is appended to that text on one line. The parent therefore matches with `contains`, not equality.

CheckRun has no Default and derives deny_unknown_fields, so adding a field forces `queued_s: None` into every literal across athena-core, athena-data and athena-cli tests. `cargo check --all-targets --locked --workspace` lists them all.
The policy scan runs only on tracked files, so a newly created file such as slots.rs must be checked for banned words by hand.

Bash and Grep cannot read the harness's persisted tool-output file because it is outside the working directory, so a large `cargo test` output cannot be re-read. An error block (`Exit code N`) appears for a failing command, and its absence is the only success signal available.
desires: A way to read a large `cargo test` output (or a filtered run) inside the working directory, to see the per-test summary instead of relying on the absence of an error.
